The history of reheated/handled food and rapid vomiting-predominant illness point most classically to Staphylococcus aureus enterotoxin (Bacillus cereus emetic toxin is an alternative consideration, classically linked to fried rice, but less likely given the nonspecific food description). Stool culture may be negative because symptoms are toxin-mediated. Vital signs show hypotension and tachycardia consistent with dehydration from vomiting/diarrhea, supporting a toxic/fluid-loss process rather than systemic infection.

DIAGNOSIS: Staphylococcus aureus food poisoning (preformed enterotoxin)
